findings.title: `fire_unit_until` still blocks until the whole minute pass ends
findings.description: `fire_unit_until()` calls `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], sudo=True, check=False, stream=True)` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:356`. That launches `deploy/mt-run`, whose `start_and_stream()` starts the unit with `--no-block` and then waits in `while is_running "${unit}"; do sleep 2; done` at `deploy/mt-run:127-129`; `subprocess.run()` therefore does not return until the oneshot finishes. As a result, `wait_for_unit_or_line()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:318-331` and `stop_unit()` at `scripts/cutover_common.py:337-339` are unreachable while the unbounded backfill is running, defeating the new "stop once the trailing phase line lands" behavior described in `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:174-182`. The interactive `Ctrl-C detaches` trap at `deploy/mt-run:125` does not make Python's `subprocess.run()` keep waiting; it propagates `KeyboardInterrupt`. The new tests at `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py:441-490` patch `cutover_common.run` to return immediately, so they assert the intended control flow but not the real wrapper contract.

findings.title: Firing-time selection uses `.replace()` on a non-UTC database timestamp
findings.description: `MINUTE_PASS_FIRING_TIMES_UTC` and `deploy/systemd/mt-minute-pass.timer:7-8` define `04:05`/`13:05` UTC, but `collecting_firing_finished_at()` calls `close.replace(hour=firing.hour, minute=firing.minute, ...)` on `session.session_close_utc` without first converting it to UTC. The same file acknowledges at `src/manta_trading/cli/commands/minute_session_mass.py:260-265` that psycopg returns `timestamptz` in the connection zone (`America/Denver` in production) and fixes only the display label with `.astimezone(UTC)`. With a Denver-zone close, `04:05` is built as 04:05 MDT/MST (10:05/11:05 UTC), so the +3h verdict becomes 13:05/14:05 UTC instead of 07:05 UTC. The changed boundary tests at `test/unit/cli/commands/test_data_health.py:192-260` use UTC-aware datetimes and do not exercise the production timezone path.

findings.title: Repair/verify command failures can be reported as a complete cutover
findings.description: `_repair()` runs the production Python with `check=False`, prints a non-zero exit message, and returns only `stdout + stderr`. `_verify_when_fresh()` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:200-213` and `main()` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:264-273` decide acceptance solely from the absence of `"FAIL"` and `"[WAIT]"` in that text. A crashed `--verify` (traceback, DB/connection error, or the `RepairScanTimeout` branch in `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py#main`, which prints `"scan refused"` and returns `EXIT_REFUSED`) contains neither marker, so the script can print `CUTOVER COMPLETE` and return 0. Non-zero `--apply`/`--check` failures are also logged but ignored before the script continues firing passes. Propagate the child return code or use a structured status instead of inferring success from free-form output.

findings.title: The sudoers policy is inconsistent with the cutover commands and is not least-privilege
findings.description: The file claims at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:1-4` to allow "exactly the commands those scripts issue, nothing wider", but `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:97-99` issues `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py ...` and no alias permits that command. Conversely, `MT_RUN *` at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:8` permits arbitrary arguments to the root-executed wrapper; `deploy/mt-run:148-166` passes those arguments through to `/opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/mt` after sourcing the production env file. `MT_INSTALL` at `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops:9` also grants NOPASSWD root to a script under the operator's home checkout; if that path is writable by `manta`, it is an arbitrary-root grant. Install the privileged installer to a root-owned path, enumerate exact repair commands, and avoid the broad `mt-run *` rule.

findings.title: The new cutover log does not contain the actual cutover report
findings.description: `start_log()`/`say()` tee only `say(...)` lines. The repair script's acceptance output is emitted with `print(output)` at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:102`; pass streaming output and the polling lines in `scripts/cutover_common.py:318-331` are also plain `print` or inherited stdout. That contradicts the script docstring at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:21` ("every action is logged") and the `full narration` label at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:278`: the file misses the PASS/FAIL/WAIT numbers and journal output that motivated the log. `test/unit/test_cutover_921.py:501-508` only proves two `say()` lines are written, not that the report is auditable.

findings.title: Session judgement counts bars that ingestion will discard
findings.description: `bar_timestamp()` at `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute_sessions.py:27-40` validates only the timestamp, and `sessions_without_bars()` at `:43-61` treats any parsed in-session timestamp as collected. But `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py#_bar_to_row` skips bars with missing, null, non-finite, or non-positive OHLC values before `_insert_minute_bars()` writes anything. `judge_chunk_by_sessions()` is called at `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:902-909` using the raw response bars; a single in-session bar with a valid timestamp but invalid prices can therefore produce `SUCCESS`, delete/shrink the gap row, and insert zero rows. The new fixtures in `test/unit/data/acquisition/daemon/test_minute_sessions.py:22-36` only build valid price bars. Judge the validated insertable rows (or the insert result), and add a malformed-price regression test.

findings.title: Changed import blocks violate the required Ruff import-order rule
findings.description: `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.ruff.lint]` block selects `I`, so Ruff enforces import grouping/sorting. The changed `from cutover_common import ...` block at `scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:45-58` is not sorted; neither is `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py:59-66` (`cagg_freshness_for_session, CheckReport, RepairScanTimeout, build...`), `src/manta_trading/data/acquisition/daemon/minute.py:16-64` (local application imports interleaved out of order), or `test/unit/test_repair_921.py:27-33`. These will be flagged by the mechanically enforced Ruff baseline. Run `ruff check --fix` and `ruff format` on the touched files.

findings.title: The new cagg freshness probe bypasses the guarded shared helper
findings.description: `cagg_freshness_for_session()` reimplements the refresh-job lookup with a plain `SELECT stats.last_successful_finish`, an inner `JOIN`, no `nullif(..., '-infinity'::timestamptz)`, no `scheduled`/`last_run_status` signals, and no statement timeout. The established helper at `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py:70-82` already normalizes `-infinity`, uses a `LEFT JOIN`, and `src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py#_set_probe_timeout` bounds every probe with `CAGG_FRESHNESS_PROBE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT`. `scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py#run_verify` calls this partial probe and then `fetch_session_mass()` directly without `assert_cagg_fresh`, so acceptance has a second, weaker freshness implementation. Reuse the shared verdict/augment seam or extract one bounded helper; also add a never-refreshed-policy test.
